questions.q: How does the summary describe the inner life of introverts?
a: Rich, and recharged by quiet, safe surroundings
Empty, and in need of constant stimulation
Anxious, and best ignored altogether
Shallow, and focused on social approval
questions.why: Lesson 1 says introverts have a rich inner life and recharge in quiet, safe environments.

questions.q: What does the summary say about an introvert's nervous system?
a: It is more sensitive to sounds, sights and tastes
It reacts more slowly to any stimulation
It works exactly like an extrovert's system
It needs more sleep than the average person
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites studies showing introverts are more sensitive to what goes on around them.

questions.q: What is the goal of the Think/Pair/Share technique?
a: Students think alone, discuss in pairs, then share as a class
Students compete to answer first in front of the class
Every student must speak once during the lesson
Teachers grade students on how often they raise a hand
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes time to think alone, then paired discussion, then a whole-class sharing.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend before attending a crowded event?
a: Arrive with one or two trusted friends
Prepare a list of topics to discuss
Practice small talk with strangers
Leave as soon as you feel tired
questions.why: Lesson 3 says going with a friend is far less distressing than showing up alone.

questions.q: How can an introverted athlete prepare for a team game?
a: Visualize success quietly before playing
Rely on team chants to build energy
Avoid team sports whenever possible
Wait for the coach to assign a role
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests using an introvert's focus and imagination to picture success beforehand.
